correctness.rationale: The claim specifies the uncentered probability-normalized Gram matrix on the uniform spanning-tree orbit. Differentiating a weighted reduced-Laplacian determinant gives all two-edge moments; the wheel Green kernel solves the periodic recurrence. Explicit cyclic transforms of two squared Green kernels produce every two-by-two Fourier block, including the exceptional constant block. Positivity, sharp spectral extrema, forced nullity and cubic condition asymptotic follow algebraically. Exhaustive construction of exact integer Gram matrices for each n=3,...,10 matches every predicted eigenvalue within 3e-15, with direct tree counts and trace/nullity checks. This finite evidence corroborates rather than proves the universal result.

originality.rationale: The nearest broad prior result, Burton-Pemantle (arxiv:math/0404048, Theorems 1.1 and 4.2), gives a general determinant for edge marginals but no explicit wheel coordinate-Walsh eigenvalue evaluation, low-mode singular value or condition asymptotic. Benjamin-Yerger computes wheel spanning-tree counts and a circulant Laplacian; Dall-Pfeifle gives weighted matrix-tree context. Their premises are used openly, and their published conclusions do not state or immediately quantify the asserted sharp Fourier sampling constants. Published wheel edge-polytope ellipsoid findings concern a distinct invariant and do not dominate the claim. Historical priority remains bounded and an unlocated specialist computation is a real risk.

value.rationale: The uniform spanning-tree orbit of a wheel is a canonical natural graphical-matroid base set, and degree-one Walsh characters encode the elementary edge observables. Exact sampling stability is a meaningful invariant beyond the tree count. The evaluated 2n eigenvalues identify precisely one forced dependence, a two-dimensional extremal low cyclic mode for all n>=4 and a sharp cubic Gram condition ratio with an explicit asymptotic constant. These structural features are neither routine reparametrizations nor consequences of the ordinary spanning-tree enumeration alone; they provide quantitative conditioning information for a full infinite non-series-parallel graph family.
